scenes.title: Offsets & Message Retention
scenes.subtitle: Tracking position and controlling how long data lives
scenes.narration: Offsets track where each consumer is in a partition, and retention controls how long Kafka keeps events available.

scenes.title: Offsets Explained
bullets: An offset is a sequential id per partition
Consumers commit offsets to record progress
Committed offsets live in an internal topic
Consumers can rewind or skip to any offset
scenes.narration: An offset is a monotonically increasing id assigned to every record within a partition. Consumers commit offsets to record how far they have read, so they can resume after a restart. These committed offsets are stored in the internal __consumer_offsets topic. Because offsets are just positions, a consumer can rewind to reprocess history or seek forward to skip ahead.

scenes.title: Two Ways to Clean Up
scenes.narration: Kafka offers two retention strategies. Delete-based retention drops whole log segments once they exceed a time or size limit, which suits ordinary event streams. Log compaction instead keeps only the most recent value for each key, which is ideal for changelogs and stateful snapshots. You choose per topic with the cleanup.policy setting.

scenes.title: Configuring Retention
scenes.code:
# Keep data for 7 days
kafka-configs.sh --alter \
  --bootstrap-server localhost:9092 \
  --entity-type topics --entity-name orders \
  --add-config retention.ms=604800000

# Enable compaction on a changelog topic
kafka-configs.sh --alter \
  --bootstrap-server localhost:9092 \
  --entity-type topics --entity-name user-state \
  --add-config cleanup.policy=compact
scenes.narration: The first command sets the orders topic to retain events for seven days, expressed as milliseconds. Once records age past that window, their segments become eligible for deletion. The second command switches a user-state topic to compaction, so Kafka keeps only the latest record per key indefinitely. Retention is a per-topic setting, letting you tune each stream to its purpose.

scenes.text: Retention is independent of consumption. Kafka keeps data until the policy says otherwise, so multiple consumers can read the same events at different times.
scenes.narration: Remember that retention is independent of consumption. Kafka keeps data until the policy says otherwise, which is exactly what lets multiple consumers read the same events at their own pace.
